legacy.full_text: 我有个问题一直不能理解，如果 A 模型蒸馏了 B 模型，那 A 模型能超越 B 模型吗？还是说从理论上就不可以？

text:
因为不同模型厂商之前预训练的轨迹和看到的信息不一样，所以在后训练时候所谓的“蒸馏”更多的是将一些策略(policy) 给对齐出来，而不是从老师那里获取纯监督方案。

只有纯小模型做学生，纯相同数据集，纯理论上的 logits 蒸馏，才有确定的老师上限，其余情况没有理论支撑，而且实践中全都是反例。

用人类的例子也很容易理解的：学生超过老师的比比皆是，因为蒸馏达成的知识转化是所有学习能力的一方面而已。

text:
有个研究生，一周解决了一道五十年没搞定的数学难题。因为她压根没觉得那算正经研究。

她叫丽莎·皮奇里洛，2018年在德州大学奥斯汀分校读研。一次会议上听说了"康威结"，晚上回去就开始琢磨。

用她自己的话说：白天她不允许自己碰这个，觉得这不是真正的数学，有点像做作业。

这个问题从六十年代就没人解出来。十二个交叉点及以下的结，所有"切片性"都被数学家们确定完了，就差这一个。剑桥大学牛顿数学研究所大门上，甚至有这个结的雕塑。

她一周就把它破了。

方法才是真的漂亮。她不直接攻康威结，而是构造了另一个结，和康威结共享同一条四维轨迹。然后证明她造的那个结不是切片结。因为两个结轨迹相同、切片状态也相同，康威结自然也不是。

完事之后，她随口跟资深拓扑学家卡梅伦·戈登提了一句。戈登直接喊起来："你怎么一点都不激动？"说这玩意儿马上能上《数学年刊》。

确实上了。研究生毕业十四个月后，她去了MIT。

而她们这个领域之所以存在，原因本身就挺奇妙的。

四维是唯一会"崩塌"的维度。平坦的n维空间，每个n都有且仅有一个光滑结构。唯独四维，有不可数无穷多个。

不是三维，不是五维，不是十一维。就四维。

到现在也没人完全搞清楚为什么。

text:
我表弟退房时，前台拿着一张照片，说房间里的纸巾盒少了一个角，要扣 680 块。

那是个黑色木盒，边上有块指甲盖大的缺口。

孩子前一天拿着它在地上推过两圈，表弟媳当时就看见了，还让孩子放回去。她以为最多赔个纸盒钱，没想到前台递来的是维修报价单。

表弟没吵，先让前台调门锁记录和保洁交接单。

对方说，入住前房间检查过，没有问题。

表弟又让他们把检查照片找出来。前台翻了十几分钟，只找出一张铺好床的远景，纸巾盒正好被台灯挡住。

经理过来，说这是定制家具，整个台面都得换。

表弟把手机放到柜台上，给经理看自己刚入住时拍给孩子母亲的视频。孩子在镜头里爬上床，桌上的纸巾盒边角已经缺了一小块。

经理看完没说话，转身进了办公室。

二十分钟后，前台把 680 块撤掉了，只收了 60 块清洁费。

表弟拿回房卡时，前台小声说，昨天还有一家也被扣了这个钱。

他没走，站在柜台边把视频转给了那家人。

text:
今天 GitHub 被万能 Agent 屠榜了！

5 个星标暴增最狠的项目，专业拆解下：

1.  Panniantong/Agent-Reach

给 AI Agent 装上全网眼睛。Twitter、Reddit、YouTube、GitHub、B 站、小红书……一键读取，零 API 费用，自愈路由

🔗 直达：https://t.co/vn7mtGSzjW

以前 Agent 被关在笼子里，现在直接打开整个互联网。情报战时代真正落地！

2.  Leonxlnx/taste-skill

给 AI 装上「审美品味」。告别千篇一律的 slop 前端，强制布局、字体、动效、密度全部升级。

🔗 直达：https://t.co/N1WiUkLeec

终于不用再看 Agent 生成的塑料感 UI 了，直接出有设计感的作品。前端生产力质变！

3.  calesthio/OpenMontage

世界首个开源 Agentic 视频制作系统。12 条流水线 + 52 种工具，描述一句话，Agent 自己研究、写脚本、生成素材、剪辑出片。

🔗 直达：https://t.co/ZnDldYbJsD

一个人顶整个视频团队，含金量直接爆表。

4.  microsoft/markitdown

微软亲儿子级文档预处理神器。PDF / Word / PPT / Excel / 音视频一键转干净 Markdown，专为 LLM 喂料设计。

🔗 直达：https://t.co/YXF5hHyosg

Agent 吃料再也不用手动清洗了，预处理层事实标配。

5.  DeusData/codebase-memory-mcp 
把整个代码库变成持久知识图谱的 MCP 服务器。Agent 再也不用每次重新「读」项目。

🔗 直达：https://t.co/tKcy97ddua

长期项目记忆终于有了真正可用的基础设施。

//

总结

2026 年的风口已经是「Agent 可插拔能力层」。谁先把这些项目玩透，谁就站在下一波生产力革命的 C 位。

quotedTweet.text:
今天 GitHub 被逆向 Agent 彻底刷屏了！

5 个星标暴增、真正能落地的硬核项目，专业拆解下：

1.  diegosouzapw/OmniRoute
 免费 MIT AI 网关：一个 endpoint 通吃 290+ 供应商（90+ 免费额度）、500+ 模型，配额感知自动 fallback + 强压缩，直接兼容 Claude Code / Cursor / OpenCode / Cline。
 🔗 直达：https://t.co/z4qcJNrGWm
 以前切模型像换 VPN，现在一个 endpoint 通吃，token 成本直接腰斩。网关赛道新王！

2.  Optim-Agent/optim-agent
 把 LLM Agent 变成超参数优化器，自动帮你调模型、调工作流、调 prompt。
 🔗 直达：https://t.co/S6X4xfWF7r
 以前调参靠玄学，现在 Agent 自己跑实验、自己收敛。MLOps + Agent 的完美交叉点！

3.  zhaoxuya520/reverse-skill
 AI 逆向 / 渗透 / 安全研究技能路由包。自动路由方法论 + 按需自举工具链 + 自进化知识库，原生支持 Claude Code、Cursor、Cline 等一众 Agent。
 🔗 直达：https://t.co/Uk4X2fgO6S
 以前安全研究像手动堆工具箱，现在 Agent 自己挑刀、自己进化经验库。硬核到爆！

4.  huggingface/speech-to-speech 本地语音 Agent 管道（VAD → STT → LLM → TTS），OpenAI Realtime 兼容，组件全可换，支持实时打断与工具调用。
 🔗 直达：https://t.co/9R5NCNWdnx
 真正能本地跑起来的实时语音对话 Agent，隐私和延迟双赢，开源玩家狂喜！

5.  lyogavin/airllm
 单卡 4GB 就能跑 70B（甚至更大），层式加载，无需量化蒸馏。支持 Llama / Qwen / DeepSeek 等主流模型。
 🔗 直达：https://t.co/2T1mqCJc8g
 显卡乞丐也能养起大模型 Agent 的神器，本地推理直接起飞！

//

总结

2026 年的风口已经从“会聊天的模型”全面转向“能干活、能进化、能本地落地的 Agent 基建”。谁先把这些玩透，谁就站在下一波生产力 C 位。

text:
不到 1000 万美金，你根本不需要选股

散户有一个挺普遍的误区：账户里有几万几十万美金，就开始琢磨怎么在二十只股票之间做配置。

我的看法很直接。1000万美金以内，选股这件事对你没有价值。要么全买指数ETF，要么就买当下最主流、流动性最好的那几只。中间那些花大量时间挖出来的「性价比标的」，反而是最没必要的部分。

因为分散持仓从来不是一个赚钱手段，它是机构的合规产物。

基金有受托责任，有单一持仓上限，有风控条款，有季度赎回压力。一只票拿到组合的15%，风控就该找你谈话了。它们不是不想集中，是不被允许集中。而你没有出资人，没有合规部，没有人在季度末拿回撤考核你。把机构的约束条件当成投资智慧抄过来，等于自愿戴上一副别人被迫戴的镣铐。

规模这一层更实际。

机构真正的难处是建仓本身就在推价格，清仓本身就在砸坑。几百亿的基金想买一只中盘股，得分几周慢慢吸，卖的时候还要担心那根大阴线是自己画出来的。所以它必须把钱摊到几十上百个标的上。

1000万美金放在主流大票里是什么概念？开盘一分钟进出，盘口不会有任何反应。冲击成本这个问题对你不存在。既然约束不存在，为这个约束设计的解决方案自然也不需要。

最后一点是最多人栽的地方：一个人管不了那么多仓位。

持仓超过十只，你不可能对每只都保持真实认知。财报看不完，消息跟不上，某只跌了20%你不知道该加还是该砍，涨上去也说不清该不该走。手里握的最后是一堆自己不了解的代码。

而且这种分散往往是假的。二十只票里可能十八只跑的是同一个beta，你以为在对冲风险，其实只是把同一个赌注拆成二十份下，还多付了二十倍的注意力。

所以要么承认自己不做研究，SPY、QQQ买了躺着；要么就集中在你真看得懂、成交量足够大的少数几只上。

稀缺的从来不是标的，是你能持续跟踪的注意力。

#美股 #投资理财 #ETF #指数基金 #仓位管理

text: 美元霸权体系的裂痕已经深深不可弥补了。白宫TACO，默许伊朗在海峡收费，财政部网站撤下了所有对伊朗的制裁，贝森特谎称协议达成，两天内公布，美国救助日元汇率。这一切都是为了挽救美债的颓势。全部效果持续了不到一个星期就以失败告终。美债继续疲软，韩国央行加入购金大军，阿根廷不管美国的压力，继续和中国续签货币互换协议，中国人民币离岸主权债券发行需求强劲。不是人民币变强，恰恰相反，中国最近的很多政策不利于人民币国际化，而是在比烂的世界里，美元体系和信用出了大问题。不是我觉得怎么样，而是市场已经用真金白银投票，包括美国的盟友和对手都已经投出了不信任票。虽然美元的国际地位短期不会被超越，但是加速下滑的态势已不可避免。必须要认清宏观大趋势，不被政客的嘴炮欺骗。美联储和财政部正在玩狼来了的游戏，而市场越来越不买账。我们要确保在“两个阶段，三步走”的最后一步，债务货币化全面开花的环境中，我们的财富不会重大缩水。

text:
🤯 LightRAG v1.5.5 is now live — built to handle messy documents, long-running indexing, and the realities of production RAG.

Five weeks since our last release, we’ve merged 150 PRs and welcomed 16 new contributors. This release focuses on smarter document understanding, production-grade reliability, concurrency, and security.

📄 Smart Heading: Recover the true structure of messy Word documents

Real-world DOCX files rarely have clean heading hierarchies:
- Headings may be missing outline levels
- Body text may accidentally retain heading styles
- Heading levels may be inverted or skipped
- Merged documents may contain conflicting structures

When chunking relies on these unreliable signals, chunks no longer follow semantic boundaries—splitting related context and reducing retrieval quality.

Smart Heading reconstructs the document’s intended structure by:
- Recovering missing section headings
- Reclassifying body text incorrectly styled as headings
- Repairing inverted or skipped heading levels
- Detecting boundaries between merged documents
- Reducing noise from excessively long tables of contents

Smart Heading is available as an optional capability in the Native DOCX parser and must be explicitly enabled.

🔧 Production hardening
- 🧠 Bounded memory — Pipeline RSS no longer grows continuously with workload, enabling stable long-running batch indexing.

- 🔁 Reliable recovery — Write-ahead anchors, chunk logs, and scan-based rollback restore a consistent state after interruptions.

- ⚡ Stronger concurrency — Shared storage reduces cross-process RPC, key locks support cancellation and dead-process recovery, and pipelines now provide workspace-level isolation.

- 🔒 Security fixes — Six security advisories addressed, covering login brute force, password-comparison timing attacks, stored XSS, SSRF bypasses, and ReDoS.

- 🖥️ Also included
WebUI server response time and time-to-first-token metrics, a parser capability matrix, graph-rendering and auto-scroll fixes, configurable file suffixes for MinerU and Docling, plus numerous edge-case fixes across parsing, retrieval, storage, and APIs.

A smarter, safer, and more reliable LightRAG for production workloads.

📦 Release: https://t.co/hYKfv2pbS2
🔗 GitHub: https://t.co/6FVovsQCWs

result.text:
🤯 LightRAG v1.5.5 is now live — built to handle messy documents, long-running indexing, and the realities of production RAG.

Five weeks since our last release, we’ve merged 150 PRs and welcomed 16 new contributors. This release focuses on smarter document understanding, production-grade reliability, concurrency, and security.

📄 Smart Heading: Recover the true structure of messy Word documents

Real-world DOCX files rarely have clean heading hierarchies:
- Headings may be missing outline levels
- Body text may accidentally retain heading styles
- Heading levels may be inverted or skipped
- Merged documents may contain conflicting structures

When chunking relies on these unreliable signals, chunks no longer follow semantic boundaries—splitting related context and reducing retrieval quality.

Smart Heading reconstructs the document’s intended structure by:
- Recovering missing section headings
- Reclassifying body text incorrectly styled as headings
- Repairing inverted or skipped heading levels
- Detecting boundaries between merged documents
- Reducing noise from excessively long tables of contents

Smart Heading is available as an optional capability in the Native DOCX parser and must be explicitly enabled.

🔧 Production hardening
- 🧠 Bounded memory — Pipeline RSS no longer grows continuously with workload, enabling stable long-running batch indexing.

- 🔁 Reliable recovery — Write-ahead anchors, chunk logs, and scan-based rollback restore a consistent state after interruptions.

- ⚡ Stronger concurrency — Shared storage reduces cross-process RPC, key locks support cancellation and dead-process recovery, and pipelines now provide workspace-level isolation.

- 🔒 Security fixes — Six security advisories addressed, covering login brute force, password-comparison timing attacks, stored XSS, SSRF bypasses, and ReDoS.

- 🖥️ Also included
WebUI server response time and time-to-first-token metrics, a parser capability matrix, graph-rendering and auto-scroll fixes, configurable file suffixes for MinerU and Docling, plus numerous edge-case fixes across parsing, retrieval, storage, and APIs.

A smarter, safer, and more reliable LightRAG for production workloads.

📦 Release: https://t.co/hYKfv2pbS2
🔗 GitHub: https://t.co/6FVovsQCWs

text:
The $150,000 rugpull we warned everybody about.

A grey-market peptide "group buy" running under the Peptide University brand collapsed this week, and the members who funded it are out around $150,000. The usual story when one of these blows up is that some anonymous Chinese lab took the money and went dark. That is not what happened here. We pulled the transactions off the blockchain and followed them to their destination: Binance and OKX.

The setup took months. A promoter named Eric Ranks built himself up as the community's testing authority, the guy who supposedly vetted vendors, and then pointed buyers at a vendor called "Bella." The lab certificates Bella handed out do not survive a look. Several verify to entirely different companies, Tianjin Eleli and Novara Peptides among them. Others fail verification on the testing lab's own website. Asked about it, Ranks said the testing had been done "by customers." It had not. Buyers were shown other vendors' certificates with Bella's name pasted on.

When Bella fell apart, the same people ran it again. A figure who never showed his face, "Mr. Based," collected members' money into pooled buys that went straight into his personal crypto wallet, and lined up a replacement vendor, RX Anabolics, that other communities had already called out as a scam months earlier.

The money is where it stops being he-said-she-said. Roughly $178,000 moved out of Mr. Based's collection wallet. About $107,000 of it went to a "vendor" wallet and from there into Binance. Another $57,000 went to OKX. The vendor wallet had itself been funded, in the first place, from Coinbase.

Coinbase, Binance and OKX are American-reachable exchanges that collect government ID. A real overseas vendor stays as far from them as possible, for obvious reasons. These deposit addresses are public, they are sitting on the chain right now, and each one resolves to an account with a real name behind it. Whoever ends up asking the exchanges knows exactly which door to knock on.

One detail ties the whole thing together. The people running these buys spend a remarkable amount of energy attacking the one thing that would expose them, which is independent lab testing. A test a product passed gets recast as a lie. Certificates of analysis get dismissed as a waste of time. The members who keep asking for them get muted, then banned.

If you spend money in this corner of the market: verify every certificate yourself on the testing lab's own site instead of trusting a PDF, treat a missing batch or lot number as a missing test, and be very wary of any large group buys, especially from bald cartoon internet figures and obese pretend entrepreneurs. A vendor who bans the people asking for lab reports has already told you what you needed to know.

The full investigation, with more than 40 exhibits and the complete transaction trail, is here: https://t.co/TtNAhGL4FH

Your contract review agent can read an NDA and summarize the key terms. But ask it "what are the risky clauses?" and you get a different answer every time.

Neither gets solved by a bigger model.

Here's a deep dive of the Box AI Extract NDA risk workflow. 

The agent calls POST /2.0/ai/extract_structured with a fixed five-field schema: governing law, term, termination, confidentiality period, liability cap. Confidence scores and source references included. A transparent rule set scores each clause automatically. 

The Deal Risk Summary saves back to Box as a companion file alongside the source document. Same output shape every time, regardless of how the document is written.

Extract, don't prompt.

The problem with this Iran deal isn’t only the nuclear fine print. It’s the signal it sends. Washington starts a war, scrambles into a ceasefire, leaves the most important nuclear questions for later, talks about a reconstruction fund, and then insists it still “has all the cards.” But the regional powers are watching something very different: they are watching America spend blood, money, credibility, and leverage , then emerge with an opaque agreement whose hardest issues are postponed. Reuters reports that the MOU framework leaves Iran’s nuclear program for a 60-day negotiation period and that the full text has not yet been released.  

And while Washington is busy selling this as a win, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Turkey, and Pakistan are already testing the outlines of a new regional security coordination mechanism. Pakistan’s Foreign Ministry confirmed a quadrilateral meeting of Egypt, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey on the sidelines of the Riyadh ministerial talks, and regional analysts describe repeated coordination among these states as an emerging security partnership rather than a formal alliance, but that distinction is exactly the point. It does not need to be NATO on day one. It only needs to become a habit.    

Once those countries start coordinating security, ceasefires, maritime access, missile threats, energy flows, and diplomatic channels among themselves, the United States is no longer the indispensable broker. It becomes a vendor. A weapons vendor. A sanctions vendor. A crisis-management consultant with aircraft carriers. That is a catastrophic downgrade from being the power everyone must go through.

And sitting behind that shift is China. Not necessarily with tanks or bases, but with diplomacy, trade, credit, infrastructure, energy demand, and quiet leverage. Beijing already hosted and sponsored the 2023 Saudi-Iran normalization talks, and the joint statement explicitly tied China to restored Saudi-Iranian relations and security/economic cooperation frameworks.   Carnegie and Stimson analyses have also noted that China’s Middle East posture is built around mediation credibility, energy interests, investment, and balancing relations with both Saudi Arabia and Iran.    

So no, genius, this is not just “Israel is mad” or “Iran got a bad deal” or “oil prices moved for a day.” The deeper issue is that America’s enemies and partners are learning the same lesson at the same time: Washington can be bypassed. Iran can be managed through regional mediators. Gulf security can be discussed without waiting for Washington. Turkey can act as a regional organizer. Pakistan can serve as a bridge to both the Gulf and China. Egypt can regain relevance through Arab security coordination. Saudi Arabia can hedge between American protection, Chinese economics, and regional self-help.

That is how American primacy dies, not with one dramatic announcement, but with a dozen countries quietly deciding they need Plan B.

And once the Middle East starts building that Plan B, the message travels far beyond the Gulf. Countries across the Indo-Pacific will look at this and ask the obvious question: why bet everything on a United States that lurches from war to ceasefire to secret MOU, while China steadily presents itself as the adult in the room with money, infrastructure, patience, and diplomatic access?

That is the real disaster. Not that one ally is irritated. Not that one agreement is embarrassing. The disaster is that America may be teaching the world how to live without American leadership.

This isn’t a clever Iran deal. It’s a slow-motion transfer of strategic gravity from Washington-centered order to regional blocs with Beijing in the background, smiling, financing, mediating, and waiting.

Pakistan’s Foreign Ministry confirmed a quadrilateral meeting of Egypt, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey on the sidelines of the Riyadh ministerial talks, and regional analysts describe repeated coordination among these states as an emerging security partnership rather than a formal alliance, but that distinction is exactly the point. It does not need to be NATO on day one. It only needs to become a habit.    

Once those countries start coordinating security, ceasefires, maritime access, missile threats, energy flows, and diplomatic channels among themselves, the United States is no longer the indispensable broker. It becomes a vendor. A weapons vendor. A sanctions vendor. A crisis-management consultant with aircraft carriers. That is a catastrophic downgrade from being the power everyone must go through.

And sitting behind that shift is China. Not necessarily with tanks or bases, but with diplomacy, trade, credit, infrastructure, energy demand, and quiet leverage. Beijing already hosted and sponsored the 2023 Saudi-Iran normalization talks, and the joint statement explicitly tied China to restored Saudi-Iranian relations and security/economic cooperation frameworks.   Carnegie and Stimson analyses have also noted that China’s Middle East posture is built around mediation credibility, energy interests, investment, and balancing relations with both Saudi Arabia and Iran.    

So no, genius, this is not just “Israel is mad” or “Iran got a bad deal” or “oil prices moved for a day.” The deeper issue is that America’s enemies and partners are learning the same lesson at the same time: Washington can be bypassed. Iran can be managed through regional mediators. Gulf security can be discussed without waiting for Washington. Turkey can act as a regional organizer. Pakistan can serve as a bridge to both the Gulf and China. Egypt can regain relevance through Arab security coordination. Saudi Arabia can hedge between American protection, Chinese economics, and regional self-help.

That is how American primacy dies, not with one dramatic announcement, but with a dozen countries quietly deciding they need Plan B.

And once the Middle East starts building that Plan B, the message travels far beyond the Gulf. Countries across the Indo-Pacific will look at this and ask the obvious question: why bet everything on a United States that lurches from war to ceasefire to secret MOU, while China steadily presents itself as the adult in the room with money, infrastructure, patience, and diplomatic access?

That is the real disaster. Not that one ally is irritated. Not that one agreement is embarrassing. The disaster is that America may be teaching the world how to live without American leadership.

This isn’t a clever Iran deal. It’s a slow-motion transfer of strategic gravity from Washington-centered order to regional blocs with Beijing in the background, smiling, financing, mediating, and waiting.

text:
The frustrating thing about most AI harnesses is that they’re really hard to change. It owns the agent loop, context, plugins, model calls, everything. So the second you want it to work differently, you’re patching it or forking the repo.

That never made much sense to me. In iii, the harness is just another worker. Sessions, context, model routing, queues, state, streaming, traces, shell access are all just workers. They’re all separate pieces using the same functions and triggers as everything else.

You can hook into a turn, add context, change arguments, rewrite results, require approval, swap models, or replace parts completely, just using the primitives (Worker, Function, Trigger).

No fork. No special plugin world.

The harness is part of the system. It isn’t the system.

$ iii worker add console harness

GS1 is an American open-weight AI model and governed research harness designed to complete scientific computing workflows while preserving a reproducible record of its work.  

This model will be shaped by the people who know scientific work inside and out. @ENERGY is opening a contributor program for researchers, laboratories, universities, companies, and nonprofits, and we're speaking with infrastructure partners who can add training or evaluation capacity.  

There’s still lots of work ahead, and we hope you’ll help us build in the open, starting with GS1.

Someone on Reddit just built a AAA-quality snow simulation in their browser. Using Claude Opus 5.

Millions of snow particles. A character in a robe with cloth physics. Five water-based spells that carve the terrain. A snow surfing system with a wake that throws spray into sunlight.

Every footstep displaces snow. Trails form berms at the edges. Trenches slowly refill over time. Spells leave permanent craters.

The entire thing runs in one browser tab. WebGPU. No game engine. No 3D modeling software. Just code.

He wrote one detailed prompt. Opus 5 planned the architecture, wrote the shaders, built the physics, iterated from screenshots, and documented every decision.

9 hours. ~4 million tokens. You can open it right now and walk around in it.

This isn't a demo. This is the kind of thing a small studio would spend months building.

text:
The Quiet Strength of a Great Woman 

Part II

Her Quiet Strength

A woman’s greatest strength is not found in how loudly she speaks,
but in how deeply she loves.

She brings calm where there is chaos.
Hope where there is doubt.
Courage where there is fear.

The world may never notice the quiet sacrifices she makes,
yet they become the foundation upon which families, dreams, and futures are built.

True strength does not always wear armor.
Sometimes, it wears kindness, patience, and unwavering loyalty.

And those who are blessed to walk beside such a woman
know that her quiet strength is one of life’s greatest gifts.

But the sadest part of such great woman is their actual patience to a man 
No matter how much love she has and keeps silen, waiting for that moment which she still doesn’t know, most great woman lose the one who might of been her knight and shinny armour 

Sources:
The Holy Bible — Proverbs 12:4 (“An excellent wife is the crown of her husband.”)
The Holy Bible — Proverbs 31:10–31 (the virtuous woman)
The Holy Bible — Ecclesiastes 4:9–12 (“Two are better than one…”)
The Holy Bible — Ephesians 5:21–33 (mutual love, respect, and self-sacrifice in marriage)
The Holy Bible — 1 Corinthians 13:4–8 (the nature of love)

A great read as well 
Aristotle, Nicomachean Ethics, Books VIII–IX (on friendship, virtue, and companionship)

text:
When we partnered with Bubble, their original vision wasn't to build a network of agencies like RapidDev.

It was the opposite: give people the tools to build for themselves.

So when I got asked whether agencies still make sense in a world where AI can spin up software for anyone, I gave the honest answer.

People will always hire vendors.

I was on a walk-and-talk with a guy still selling websites for $10K. It doesn't matter how good the technology gets, there's an asymmetry of information. Busy owners don't want to learn the tools. They want the expert who's done it a thousand times, who knows how to structure a site, write the copy, get it right.

Prices will collapse on the commodity end. That's already happening.

But there will always be clients who want a professional job, and don't mind paying for it.

That's the lane we're doubling down on at RapidDev. And it's why our bet on Bubble keeps paying off.
